question: Type I endometrial carcinoma (endometrioid adenocarcinoma) arises from an oestrogen-driven hyperplasia–carcinoma sequence and is associated with obesity, nulliparity, and late menopause, whereas Type II (serous/clear cell) is unrelated to oestrogen exposure and carries a worse prognosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The two-type model of endometrial carcinoma is high-yield. Type I (endometrioid, oestrogen-driven, good prognosis) vs Type II (serous/clear cell, oestrogen-independent, p53 mutation, poor prognosis) is a classic exam distinction.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Type I is oestrogen-dependent: endometrioid histology, preceded by atypical hyperplasia, low grade, better prognosis. Type II is oestrogen-independent: serous or clear-cell histology, arises in atrophic endometrium, p53 mutation, high grade, poor prognosis.
